---
title: "Sample spaces"
---

We sample one annotated interrogative-pronoun token from a finite corpus extract. What, exactly, can happen? The **outcome-representation problem** is the need to decide whether an outcome is a token, a surface form, a lemma, or an annotated lemma–relation combination before assigning probabilities.

We use the [UD Turkish BOUN source introduced on the Zipf page](zipfs-law.qmd). The teaching extract retains tokens whose annotated lemma is *hangi* ‘which’, *kim* ‘who’, or *ne* ‘what’ and whose Universal Dependencies relation is [`nsubj`](https://universaldependencies.org/u/dep/nsubj.html) or [`obj`](https://universaldependencies.org/u/dep/obj.html). One row is one annotated token nested in a sentence. The preparation filters source annotations and adds binary indicators; it does not infer filler–gap dependencies or recode relations. This finite extract contains `r nrow(read.csv("data/ud-turkish-boun/question-core-arguments.csv"))` tokens.

```{r}
#| label: load-question-tokens
library(ggplot2)

wh <- read.csv(
  "data/ud-turkish-boun/question-core-arguments.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)
wh$outcome_id <- paste(wh$split, wh$sentence_id, wh$token_id, sep = ":")

stopifnot(
  nrow(wh) == 167L,
  !anyDuplicated(wh$outcome_id),
  setequal(unique(wh$lemma), c("hangi", "kim", "ne")),
  setequal(unique(wh$dependency_relation), c("nsubj", "obj")),
  all(wh$object == (wh$dependency_relation == "obj")),
  all(wh$ne_lemma == (wh$lemma == "ne"))
)

head(wh[c("outcome_id", "form", "lemma", "dependency_relation")])
```

## Outcomes and the sample space

Basically, an outcome is one represented result, and a sample space collects every result the probability experiment allows. More specifically, an [**outcome**](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-intro.html) is one possible result represented by a probability model. The **sample space** $\Omega$ is the set of all such outcomes.

Our experiment is uniform sampling of one row from the finite extract. If $N$ is the number of retained rows, then

$$
\Omega
\equiv
\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_N\},
$$

where $\omega_i$ is the token identified by its split, sentence ID, and token ID. The category map

$$
c(\omega_i)
\equiv
\langle L_i,R_i\rangle
$$

records lemma $L_i\in\{\textit{hangi},\textit{kim},\textit{ne}\}$ and dependency relation $R_i\in\{\texttt{nsubj},\texttt{obj}\}$. Every one of the six lemma–relation combinations is attested.

```{r}
#| label: inspect-question-outcomes
category_counts <- as.data.frame(
  xtabs(~ lemma + dependency_relation, data = wh)
)
names(category_counts)[3] <- "tokens"

stopifnot(
  nrow(category_counts) ==
    length(unique(wh$lemma)) * length(unique(wh$dependency_relation)),
  all(category_counts$tokens > 0),
  sum(category_counts$tokens) == nrow(wh)
)

category_counts
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-question-outcomes
#| fig-cap: "Observed token counts in the six lemma–relation categories of the finite extract."
ggplot(category_counts,
       aes(lemma, tokens, fill = dependency_relation)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(nsubj = "grey", obj = "steelblue")) +
  labs(x = "Annotated lemma", y = "Tokens", fill = "UD relation") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

## Membership and granularity

The notation $x\in\Omega$ says that $x$ is a member of the sample space. A row key observed in the extract belongs to $\Omega$; a new string not present as a retained token does not.

```{r}
#| label: check-outcome-membership
observed_key <- wh$outcome_id[[1]]
unobserved_key <- "test:not-a-sentence:1"

c(
  observed = observed_key %in% wh$outcome_id,
  unobserved = unobserved_key %in% wh$outcome_id
)
```

The statement that the second key is outside $\Omega$ concerns this finite probability experiment. It does not claim that Turkish cannot contain another interrogative-pronoun token.

Changing granularity changes the sample space. If outcomes were lemma types, the space would contain the three observed lemmas. If outcomes were lemma–relation categories, it would contain six observed categories. Neither space preserves sentence-level identity. We keep token outcomes because the empirical measure on later pages counts rows while retaining the sentence and register identifiers that reveal dependence.

## Omission and impossibility

An omitted outcome is not an impossible linguistic result. The extract excludes interrogatives in relations other than `nsubj` and `obj`, and it excludes other interrogative lemmas. Thus its sample space describes a restricted annotated population. It is not an inventory of every interrogative expression in Turkish.

This restriction has a useful consequence and a serious limit. It gives a transparent finite experiment for probability calculations, but it licenses only statements about uniform sampling from the retained extract. Sentences, not isolated tokens, were sampled from five registers, and the treebank is not a probability sample of Turkish usage.

$\Omega$ records the model's answer to “what could happen?” The [next page](events.qmd) groups these token outcomes into events that answer linguistic questions.

## Check your understanding

1. Use `wh` to give the observation key for the first token. Which three columns form it?
2. Use `category_counts` to identify the least frequent lemma–relation category. Does its low count make it absent from $\Omega$?
3. Construct the sample space of observed lemma types. Which information in the token outcome space does this coarser space discard?
4. Why would adding all Turkish interrogative forms to the list, without adding observations, define a different probability experiment?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. The first observation key is `train:ess_1258:2`, formed from `split`, `sentence_id`, and `token_id`. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The least frequent category is *hangi*–`obj`, with one token; its low count does not remove that observed token from $\Omega$. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. The coarser sample space is $\{\textit{hangi},\textit{kim},\textit{ne}\}$, which discards token identity, sentence and register information, and dependency relation. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. Adding unobserved Turkish interrogative forms would enlarge the declared sample space beyond the 167 retained token outcomes and thus define a different probability experiment. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>
